newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise board backs merger with Suez.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise board backs merger with Suez.

text.p: French utilities group Lyonnaise des Eaux SA said on Thursday its board was unanimously in favour of a merger with holding company Cie de Suez.
"The board received it favourably and unanimously agreed in principle," it said in a statement with its 1996 results. The board met on Wednesday afternoon.
The board of Suez earlier this week also gave unanimous backing in principle to the merger, due to be discussed at the special board meetings of the two groups on April 11.

Both companies have declined comment on the terms of the merger, though Suez has said it will make an exceptional dividend payment to its existing shareholders, for an unspecified amount, to reflect capital gains made last year.
The dividend payment was seen by analysts as a sweetener to persuade Suez's shareholders to back the merger.
Lyonnaise also said it made a net attributable profit last year of 1.35 billion francs, compared to 906 million in 1995 on sales of 91.6 billion compared to 85.8 billion.
Analysts had said they expected a net attributable profit for 1996 of between 1.0 billion and 1.5 billion francs.
Lyonnaise said it was looking forward to further growth in business and profitability during 1997.
